initial:
Use case: precise-object-edit / modular level-map illustration.
Input 1 is the edit target and EXACT art style to retain: a dark Chinese underworld modular 4-tile landscape. Input 2 is ONLY a game-design reference showing how a winding route spreads level selection buttons up and down the map. DO NOT copy the second image's parchment palette, cartoon characters, text, menus or interface.

Edit the FIRST image to replace the nearly straight horizontal road with a MUCH MORE WINDING MAIN ROAD, suitable for placing large level-selection buttons along it. Retain the moody charcoal painted mountains, gray mist, twisted dead trees, warm red lanterns, muted red river, Chinese gates, stone bridge, rope bridge and final palace. Maintain canvas 2172 x 724, EXACT four equal 543 x 724 tiles side by side, same overall art detail. No borders, seams, divider lines, panel labels, text, baked-in buttons or UI.

Critical layout: 1 is an entrance cap, 4 is the ending palace. Tile 2 and tile 3 must both connect to either other tile or themselves in ANY order (1[23]*4). Keep each connectable tile edge's outermost 72px as quiet gray landscape and a HORIZONTAL ROAD CENTERED AT y=450 with width about 30px. Ports at x543,1086,1629 all have matching clouds, far mist, terrain, cliff silhouette, brightness and road height. Do not let large props or branches cross ports. Road curves only within each tile's interior, then returns level to y450 at its edge.

Inside each tile, create a SINGLE CLEAR UNBROKEN MAIN ROUTE with broad S-curves and switchbacks, spreading across a large VERTICAL range from about y290 to y560. Make the road clearly visible, medium-width muted dusty reddish stone, not a tiny background trail. Widen the surrounding terrain near several road bends into unobstructed flat places where the game can later overlay 55px diameter level buttons. Leave space above those places for labels. These are ordinary natural rocky clearings, NOT manufactured circular pads. No drawn button outlines. Do not add a straight bypass, fork, intersecting roads or dead-end side routes. The winding route must be the only main traversal from entry to exit.

Tile-specific route intent (coordinates are LOCAL to each 543x724 tile, x grows left to right, y measured from top):
Tile 1: entry gate near (95,340); road descends in a wide curve toward (180,530), then rises through (300,350), then curves through (400,400) to the right port at (543,450). Two pronounced gentle bends, with three or four clear landmark/button spaces along it.
Tile 2: enter (0,450), stay level until x72; curve UP through (160,330) and (245,300); cross a stone arch bridge along the route; curve DOWN through (335,520) and (405,535); curve back to (471,450) then exit (543,450). Strong readable large S path, four or five button spaces. Crimson river and stone bridge must serve the curved route rather than force a horizontal straight road. Keep far ruins.
Tile 3: enter (0,450), stay level until x72; sweep DOWN through (155,545),(235,550), climb through a rope bridge around (290,430), sweep UP through (350,305),(410,325), return to (471,450) then exit (543,450). This alternate winding shape contrasts with tile2 and can repeat naturally. Ruined paifang in background, no side road ending at it.
Tile 4: enter (0,450), then wind DOWN toward (140,535), UP through (255,375), then curve toward (350,330), and end at the grand palace steps. Keep the red moon entirely inside tile4 and gray skies at the left connector.

Adapt terrain and bridges to support these routes naturally; preserve rich beautiful painterly visual quality. The BIG S-SHAPED MAIN ROAD is the main edit. Do not leave the old long straight horizontal road in place. No characters, no interface, no text, no borders.
